statement: Line $q$ in the $xy$-plane is perpendicular to the line with equation $3x - 2y = 7$, and the two lines have the same $y$-intercept. What is the $x$-intercept of line $q$?

choices.misconception: I made the slope negative but did not flip it, so I used $-\dfrac{3}{2}$ and got $-\dfrac{7}{3}$.
I used the slope of the given line, $\dfrac{3}{2}$, for line $q$, which makes it parallel, and got an $x$-intercept of $\dfrac{7}{3}$.
I flipped $\dfrac{3}{2}$ to $\dfrac{2}{3}$ but forgot to make it negative, so with $y = \dfrac{2}{3}x - \dfrac{7}{2}$ I got $\dfrac{21}{4}$.

hints: Rewrite $3x - 2y = 7$ in slope-intercept form to read off its slope and $y$-intercept.
A perpendicular line has the negative reciprocal slope. Write line $q$ with that slope and the same $y$-intercept, then set $y = 0$.
The given line is $y = \dfrac{3}{2}x - \dfrac{7}{2}$, so line $q$ is $y = -\dfrac{2}{3}x - \dfrac{7}{2}$. Solve $0 = -\dfrac{2}{3}x - \dfrac{7}{2}$.

solutions.reliable: From $3x - 2y = 7$, $y = \dfrac{3}{2}x - \dfrac{7}{2}$: slope $\dfrac{3}{2}$, $y$-intercept $-\dfrac{7}{2}$. Line $q$ has slope $-\dfrac{2}{3}$ and the same $y$-intercept, so $y = -\dfrac{2}{3}x - \dfrac{7}{2}$. Setting $y = 0$: $\dfrac{2}{3}x = -\dfrac{7}{2}$, so $x = -\dfrac{21}{4}$. Check: $-\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{21}{4}\right) - \dfrac{7}{2} = \dfrac{7}{2} - \dfrac{7}{2} = 0$.
